relatedSnapshot.title: Run the power dialler on each lead's record, from any smart view
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What we want

A rep opens any smart view on People, presses **Power dialler** and works the list one person at a time, on each person's own record. The call sits in a bar at the top, the person's context fills the page under it, and the outcomes stay in the same place on the right. Anyone can add six ready-made calling lists, such as New leads and No-shows, from New smart view in one click: for themselves, or for the whole team if they're an admin.

Clickable designs: Power dialler designs (15 Oct 2026). Use the State menu at the bottom right to step through every state; add `&role=member` to a link to see what a non-admin sees, or `&amd=on` for answer detection on. It's private until James shares it from the page's Share menu.

## Why

Part of ENG-15216: this is where reps start and run a session.

* This replaces the Calling page this ticket used to describe. James reviewed the designs on 15 Oct 2026 and chose no separate page: reps should see each lead's full context as they're dialled, the way Close does, and starting from a smart view has to be obvious.
* Today the session is a card on the People or Deals list, so a rep in a session never sees the record of the person they're calling. Aaron's ENG-15235 asks for the profile to open when a call connects, and this delivers that outcome.
* Starting is hard today: 14 of 16 team People views can't start the dialler at all (ENG-15236), which is why that ticket blocks this one.
* No-shows were the busiest list in the 30 days to 12 Oct 2026, with 3,957 calls against 2,541 for booked calls, but reps have to build a view by hand to work them.
* ENG-15217 shipped on 14 Oct 2026 (outcome gate, 1.5 s Undo, keys, Skip, honest voicemail wording). This ticket moves those behaviours onto the record and restyles them; it doesn't rebuild them.

## How it should work

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Today
    A[Saved view on People or Deals] --> B[Start] --> C[Session card on the list]
    C -. rep opens the record .-> D[Session card is gone]
  end
  subgraph After
    E[Any smart view, or an added calling list] --> F[Power dialler 34] --> G[Person's own record: call bar, brief, outcomes]
    G -- outcome saved, 1.5 s Undo --> H[Next person's record, already loaded]
    G -- End session --> I[Session summary]
  end
```

### People, any smart view

* The button reads **Power dialler** with the number of callable people in a green pill ("Power dialler 34"). Hovering says "Calls the 34 people in Qualified this month one after another. Each person's brief opens before they pick up." On a phone it shrinks to the icon and count.
* The arrow next to it opens: **Continue calling** ("From Name 101, 7 of 34. Stopped at 11:40 am."), **Start from scratch**, and **Settings for this session**.
* Settings for this session holds Ring twice, a line saying whether answer detection is on or off and what a voicemail will do (linking to Phone settings), Caller ID, and the ring time. The ring time shown is the session's real setting (32 s by default), not a fixed number.
* When the view can't be called, the button is disabled with the reason and a fix link, as ENG-15217 already does.

### New smart view, Calling lists tab

* New smart view gets a third tab next to AI view and Manual filters: **Calling lists** (People, for everyone). Going back is one click on AI view.
* Above the cards, **Add as Personal or Team**. Everyone can add a list as Personal, which only they see. Admins can also pick Team, which everyone on the team sees in Views. Members see Personal only, with "Admins can add lists for the whole team."
* The AI view's empty state shows "Or start from a ready-made calling list" with the three busiest lists and a "See all six calling lists" link. The left column has the same link under its own heading, and the Views menu keeps "Calling list · ready-made".
* Six cards: New leads, Due now, No-shows, Missed calls, Unconfirmed and Today's calls. Each says who is in it and in what order, the live count, and the oldest wait. **Add** creates a normal view (Personal or Team) and opens it, so Power dialler dials it. A list that's already added reads "Added · Open".
* Footer: "A list skips anyone another rep is on the phone with, anyone marked Do not contact and anyone without a phone."
* The lists' rules run on the server, because some aren't filters (a missed inbound call, no reply to a confirmation text). Missed calls reads the missed inbound calls that ENG-12494 surfaces.
* **Exits:** Do not call, Wrong number, Not interested, Lost and Closed remove a person from every list. Missed calls exits on any connected outbound call or a Called back outcome. No-shows exits on Rebooked, Lost or a new appointment.
* **One eligibility time per person,** checked when claimed and when dialled, so switching lists can't get round the team-wide 60-minute redial gap.

### The session, on the person's record

* **Session strip** (one slim row): the view and position ("Qualified this month, 7 of 34") with a progress line, then Calls, Connected and rate, Booked, Talk and Session time, Up next, the keys list and an outlined **End session**.
* **Call bar:** the one coloured thing on the page. It's white in the preview and wrap-up, and pale green only while ringing or live. It shows the name large, company and title, their local time, phone, attempt, status in words ("Name 1 in 3 s", "No answer, ringing again (2 of 2)"), the timer, and the controls: Mute, Drop voicemail (V), Pause after this one, and a red hang up. While a call is live and recording is on, a **Recording** label with a red dot sits at the top of the session.
* **Under the bar:** the lead brief (ENG-15465), with the Activity and Details tabs one click away.
* **Right column:** the outcome panel, always in the same place. Before a call it's disabled with "Outcomes open when Name 2 picks up". Under it, a **Next up** card for the person after this one.
* A 3-second preview before each dial. Today's calls is preview only: the rep starts each call.
* Moving on opens the next person's record, which is loaded before the current call ends, so there's no wait.
* No black in the session: Call now, Next now and Resume are soft green, End session is outlined, hang up is red.

### End session

A summary: calls, connected and rate, booked, session time and talk time, and each person called with their outcome. **Keep calling** goes back to the session; closing returns to the view.

### Calling settings the session has to respect

Both cases of each setting must work. Values for our sales team's workspace are from the read-only replica on 15 Oct 2026.

| Setting | Our sales team today | When on | When off |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Answer detection (whole workspace) | Off | A machine answer hangs up before the beep, logs "Voicemail, no message", skips wrap-up and moves on. | The rep hears the voicemail and presses V or picks Voicemail. |
| Ring twice (per rep) | On for all 5 reps | Re-rings only when nobody picked up or the line was busy, never a voicemail. | One ring per person. |
| Automatic next call (per rep) | On, 5 s | The outcome gate and 1.5 s Undo from ENG-15217. | The rep presses Next (N). |
| Ring time (per session) | 32 s default | Shown in session settings as set. |  |
| Recording by default (workspace) | On | A Recording label shows while the call is live. | No label. |

Answer detection was on for 2,662 outbound calls in the 30 days to 15 Oct 2026: 1,390 came back as a machine, 503 as a person, and 769 had no clear answer, which the session treats as a person.

### Manager floor

Next to rep status, each calling list shows how many people are waiting and the oldest wait.

## Design

James approved these on 15 Oct 2026. Kit screens, light theme, 1440 wide:

 <image> 

The states after a call (waiting for an outcome, paused while typing, Next with Undo, keys, and voicemail with answer detection on and off) render in the new layout like this:

 <image> 

## Decisions already made

* No separate Calling page. A session always starts from a smart view or an added calling list.
* Calling lists are normal views. Anyone can add one as Personal; admins can also add one for the Team (James, 15 Oct 2026). They're renamed, pinned or deleted from Views like any other view.
* The session shows a Recording label while a recorded call is live (James, 15 Oct 2026).
* The button says Power dialler, whether the session is new or unfinished. Continue calling lives in its menu.
* The call bar is the only tinted surface, and it's green only while a call rings or is live.
* Ring twice never re-rings a voicemail, whether it was detected or heard.

## Not doing

* What's inside the lead brief: ENG-15465.
* What each outcome does after the call: ENG-15221.
* Attempt schedules and calling hours: ENG-15222.
* Leaving a recorded voicemail: ENG-12188.
* Fixing the views that can't start the dialler: ENG-15236.

## Open questions

* **Should** ENG-15235 **close once this ships?** Recommended: yes, because the record is on screen for every call in a session. Aaron and James decide.

## Done when

- [ ] From any team People view that passes the dialler preflight, Power dialler starts a session on the first person's record, with no extra setup.
- [ ] Each next person opens on their own record within a second of the Undo window closing, with the call bar and outcome panel in the same place.
- [ ] Adding a calling list from New smart view creates a view, Power dialler dials it, and the card then reads "Added · Open".
- [ ] A member can add a calling list only as Personal, and nobody else sees it. An admin can add one as Team, and every teammate sees it in Views.
- [ ] With default recording on, a live call shows the Recording label; with it off, no label shows.
- [ ] A person marked Do not call or Wrong number never appears in any calling list.
- [ ] A person called by anyone in the last 60 minutes isn't dialled from any list.
- [ ] With answer detection on, a machine answer logs "Voicemail, no message" and moves on. With it off, the rep hears the voicemail and can press V or pick Voicemail. A test covers both.
- [ ] Ring twice re-rings a no answer once and never re-rings a voicemail.
- [ ] End session shows the summary with counts that match the calls placed.
- [ ] The manager floor shows each calling list's oldest wait.
- [ ] PostHog receives `tool.opened` for the Calling lists tab and `dialler.session_started` with the view or list name.

<details><summary>For whoever builds it</summary>

* Code at commit 28fcbd9b55: the session card is `apps/web/components/crm-v2/phone/power-dialer-session-card.tsx`, mounted from `apps/web/components/crm/power-dialer/power-dialer-workspace.tsx`, which People (`people-table.tsx`) and Deals (`deals-kanban.tsx`) render. Moving the session onto the record means the record route owns it.
* Session summary already exists: `apps/web/lib/dialer/session-summary.ts` and `use-session-summary.ts` (calls and connected). Booked and talk time are new.
* Queue building: `apps/web/lib/dialer/materialize-queue.ts`. Detected voicemail skips wrap-up via `skipDetectedVoicemail` in `apps/web/lib/dialer/panel-state.ts`. Ring twice only re-rings NoAnswer and Busy (`apps/web/lib/dialer/ring-again.ts`).
* Settings: `voice_setting.answering_machine_detection_enabled`, `dialer_user_preference` (`auto_advance_enabled`, `auto_advance_seconds`, `ring_twice_enabled`), `dialer_session.ring_timeout_sec`.
* The design kit lives in the private frontend library (branch `power-dialler-design-2026-10-12`, commits up to `c0eaa80`). The screens are `crm-call-session.tsx`, `crm-call-queues.tsx` (Power dialler button and menu), `crm-calling-lists.tsx` (the six cards) and `crm-list-controls.tsx` (New smart view's Calling lists tab). Ask James for a walkthrough.
* Related: ENG-15159 (who last contacted a prospect), ENG-15237 (the call note on the profile).

</details>

relatedSnapshot.title: Show SDRs who last contacted a prospect before they dial
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Before an SDR dials a prospect, show who last contacted them, how, when and what the note said, and warn when a teammate is calling them right now. SDRs keep calling prospects a teammate is already working, which wastes calls and annoys prospects, and reps coming from Close expect to see this at a glance. The data already exists, but the dialler drops the rep's name and a manual dial shows no warning.

## Problem

* The dialler panel shows "Last touch 20 minutes ago" with no name, channel or note, although the data carries the rep's name. The person record has no last-contacted line at all.
* The power dialler holds a 3-minute claim on each person and shows "Being called by" and the teammate's name for the next 3 people in the queue. A manual dial from a list or a person record takes no claim and shows no warning, so two reps can call the same prospect minutes apart.
* Notes themselves are fine: they sit on the person's timeline and every SDR can see them. The Closer role (45 members) can see only its own notes, which may hide SDR notes from closers.

This only helps once both reps work in Acquisity. Today the activity of the 10 reps who dial only in Close isn't in Acquisity at all; ENG-15158 covers that.

## User experience

Before and after, in the dialler panel when a teammate (here called Name 3, as an example) called 20 minutes ago:

| Today | After |
| -- | -- |
| Prospect name · Owner, Company | Prospect name · Owner, Company |
| Phone · 14:32 their time · Last touch 20 minutes ago | Phone · 14:32 their time |
| Open record | **Called by Name 3 20 min ago** · answered, 4 min |
|  | "Interested, asked for pricing. Call back Tue." |
|  | Open record |

* The same "Called by" line sits under the name in the person record header.
* On a manual dial from a list or record, the call popover shows the same line when a teammate called recently. It offers "Call anyway" and "Cancel" before dialling. If a teammate is on a live call with them, it says "Name 3 is on a call with them now".
* If the last contact is the rep themself, it says "You", and there's no warning.

## How it works

Today:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Rep dials from list or record] --> B[Call starts, no check]
  C[Power dialler] --> D[Claim person for 3 min]
  D --> E[Panel: Last touch, no name]
```

After this change:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Rep dials from list or record] --> B[NEW: check claim and last contact]
  B -- teammate recent --> C[NEW: warn, call anyway or cancel]
  B --> D[Call starts]
  D --> E[CHANGED: panel shows who, how, when]
```

## Decisions needed

* **Should a manual dial also take the same 3-minute claim as the power dialler?** Recommended: yes, so a teammate's power dialler skips that person while the call is live. Without it this is a warning only, and two reps can still click at the same second. Decider: the CRM product owner. Blocks: the manual-dial change.
* **How recent counts as "a teammate called recently"?** Recommended: 4 hours, shown as the default, set per workspace later if asked. Decider: the sales lead. Blocks: the warning rule.

## How we'll measure

`tool.opened` when the warning shows, and how often reps choose "Cancel" against "Call anyway", per week in the sales workspace. Today the count of calls to a person a teammate called in the previous 4 hours is unknown, so the first week sets the baseline. Read 2 weeks after release.

## Done when

* The dialler panel and the person header show the last rep's name, channel, time and first note line for a person a teammate called. How to check: on a preview, call a person as one user, then open them as another.
* A manual dial to a person a teammate called within the window shows the warning, and "Cancel" stops the call.
* The warning event lands in PostHog for the sales workspace.

## Implementation context

* Last touch with no name: `power-dialer-session-parts.tsx` lines 72 to 79 and 156. The panel type drops `byUserName` in `panel-state.ts`; it's present in `latest-communication-registry.ts`.
* Claims: `dialer-contact-lease-repository.ts` line 28; "Being called by" in `power-dialer-session-parts.tsx` lines 169 to 214.
* Adjacent work: ENG-14400 (filter by who last got in touch), ENG-13791 (shared communications).

relatedSnapshot.title: Show a lead brief for each person the power dialler calls
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What we want

As each person comes up in a power dialler session, the rep sees one brief, built from the person's record, that answers five questions before the call connects: who is this, why am I calling now, what happened last, where's the money, and what did they say. Nothing is clicked or typed per person, and the next person's brief is ready before the rep gets to them.

## Why

Part of ENG-15216: this fills the record page that ENG-15220 puts the session on.

* Today the session card shows one line, "Last touch 20 minutes ago", with no name, channel or note (ENG-15159). A rep who connects has to click around for context while the person is talking.
* James asked for this on 15 Oct 2026: SDRs and setters should find all the context they need on the lead they're dialling, shown automatically for each lead.
* Reps make 9.5 calls a day each on our dialler against 43.9 on Close (30 days to 12 Oct 2026). A brief that's ready on pick-up removes the reason to check the record before every dial.

## How it should work

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Today
    A[Session card] --> B[Last touch, no name] --> C[Rep opens the record mid-call]
  end
  subgraph After
    D[Person comes up] --> E[Brief built from the record, already loaded] --> F[Why now, Last touch, Deal and money, What they said]
    D --> G[Next 2 people loaded, AI summary ready]
  end
```

### Lead brief, at the top of the record during a session

Five groups, each filled from data we already store:

1. **Why now.** One reason pill and the one thing to read. Reasons are checked in this order: they wrote or called in and nobody answered (quoting their words, for example "Name 4 today 10:15"), a task due or overdue, a booked meeting coming up, then a failed or processing payment. In a calling list session, the list's own reason wins the pill ("Registered 2 h ago"), and their latest unanswered message is still the quote. Under the quote:
   * **Answer on this call:** any question in their messages.
   * **Also:** the other reasons, in quiet text.
   * **AI summary,** already open.
2. **Last touch.** The newest call, the last message we sent, the last note and the last past meeting, each with who, when and its result.
3. **Deal and money.** The open deal, its stage, value and next step. Then paid against the contract, the amount owed, processing and failed payments, and the last payment. Then open tasks on the person and on their deals, which the record timeline misses today.
4. **What they said.** Their messages, newest first, leaving out the one already quoted, then qualification fields (budget, decision maker, timeline) or form answers.
5. **Activity and Details tabs.** The full timeline and every field, one click away.

An empty group says so in words, for example "No deal yet. Booking a call creates one." A person with nothing on the record shows "Nobody has spoken to Name 5 yet. Open with who you are and why you're calling."

### Next up card

The right column shows the person after this one, with their reason and their brief already built.

### Loading

The briefs for the current person and the next two are loaded before their dial, and their AI summaries are generated ahead, so nothing loads after the person picks up.

## Design

James approved these on 15 Oct 2026. Clickable: Power dialler designs, private until James shares it. Kit screens, light theme, 1440 wide:

 <image> 

## Decisions already made

* The brief only reads data we already store. No new fields.
* The AI summary uses the existing record summary (ENG-13791), not a new model call per group.
* The Why now order above is fixed. A calling list's own reason wins the pill.
* Upcoming meetings show under Also, not under Last touch.
* Summaries are generated ahead only when the stored one is older than 24 hours or the record has new activity since it was written. We read the cost after the first week (James, 15 Oct 2026).

## Not doing

* The session layout, call bar and moving between people: ENG-15220.
* The warning before a manual dial when a teammate called recently: ENG-15218 and ENG-15159.
* What outcomes do: ENG-15221.

## Open questions

* **How do we find "Answer on this call"?** Recommended: have the record summary return the open questions in the same call, so there's one model call per person. Anuj decides, with James.
* **The AI summary often repeats the next step shown under Deal and money.** Recommended: tell the summary to leave out what the brief already shows. Anuj decides.

## Done when

- [ ] In a session, the current person's brief is on screen when their preview opens, with no click, and never later than 2 seconds after the call is answered.
- [ ] Why now picks the right reason for each case (unanswered message, task due, meeting coming up, payment problem, calling list reason). A unit test covers each.
- [ ] Open tasks on the person's deals show under Deal and money.
- [ ] A person with nothing on the record shows the empty words, and the layout keeps its shape.
- [ ] Next up shows the following person with their brief already built.
- [ ] PostHog receives `tool.opened` for the brief.

<details><summary>For whoever builds it</summary>

* Design kit (private frontend library, branch `power-dialler-design-2026-10-12`): `buildBrief({ lead, shell, queueReason })` and `LeadBriefCard` in `crm-call-brief.tsx`. The kit fixtures use real record shapes, so the grouping logic ports directly.
* Existing data at commit 28fcbd9b55: record summary in `apps/web/trpc/routers/crm/record-summary.ts` and `apps/web/components/crm-v2/record/record-summary.tsx`; payments in `apps/web/components/crm-v2/payments/payments-model.ts`; latest communication with the rep's name in `apps/web/lib/crm/latest-communication-registry.ts`.
* Related: ENG-15235 (profile on connect), ENG-15237 (the call note on the profile), ENG-15159.

</details>

relatedSnapshot.title: Power dialler refuses leads its own view still shows, and reps hear "An application error has occurred"
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Reps on the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace hear Twilio's "An application error has occurred" every few power-dialler calls, and retrying the same lead fails again. On 20 Oct 2026, 15 calls from 2 reps between 14:57 and 15:52 UTC were refused by the answer webhook with `target_not_visible` / `record_filtered_out`, with no filter drift and a matching caller ID (Axiom, from the refusal logging added in PR 7439). Example: Name 6's calls <twilio-sid> and <twilio-sid> at 15:36 and 15:37 UTC, both for the same lead, which the dialler had just claimed from his session.

Two faults:

1. The dial-time view check says the lead doesn't match the session's view, although the dialler claimed it from that same view seconds earlier. Cause to be confirmed against the read-only replica.
2. Authorization refusals reply HTTP 401, which Twilio plays as "An application error has occurred". The refusal log also reads "Non-Error object thrown", because the logged error is a plain metadata object.

## Done when

* A lead the dialler claims from a view passes the dial-time view check for the same view, proven by a test that fails on main.
* Every answer-webhook refusal after a verified Twilio signature, including `target_not_visible` and `unexpected`, replies 200 with spoken words and logs `voice_answer_replied` with status 200, proven by a test that fails on main.
* Refusal logs carry the real error name and message, not "Non-Error object thrown".
* After deploy, Axiom shows 0 `target_not_visible` refusals with `record_filtered_out` and no drift for a rep's real session.

Related: PR 7435 (spoken failures), PR 7439 (refusal logging).

relatedSnapshot.title: Add the power dialler launch button and session panel
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12173. For THIS ticket: this is the first screen reps SEE of the power dialler. A Call button appears on saved contact and deal views; clicking it starts a session and opens the session panel (open the Close links below for the exact look). The backend already exists by the time this starts; you are wiring UI onto `startSession`, `claimNext`, and `getActiveClaims`. Three things to keep straight: (1) "**being called by \[rep\]**" indicators come from polling `getActiveClaims` every 10-15 seconds, never from the 5-minute sync; (2) show THREE separate counts (rows in the view, unique people with phones, phoneless rows) because deals can share one person and some rows have nobody to call — one blended number would lie; (3) the manual **Next Call** button must work fully on its own, because the auto-advance rhythm ships in the NEXT ticket and QA tests this one standalone. Also: this ticket carries the PostHog usage-tracking requirement (use the repo's `instrument-activation-tracking` skill; done = events visible in PostHog, not just code merged). Why it matters: this is the SDR's daily cockpit.

**Size:** M/L · **Design:** needed (Name 7 CRM page 1444-65385) · **Blocked by:** ENG-12183, ENG-12184, ENG-12186, ENG-12187
**How it should look (Close reference):** the session controls and Call button on a list (images): <url> and <url>

### Overview

A rep opens a saved view (a saved, filtered list of contacts or deals), clicks Call, and a session panel appears. The panel shows who they are about to call, the queue ahead, who else on the team is already on which lead, and a Next Call button. This is the first rep-facing screen of the power dialler.

### Problem

The backend (sessions, queue, claims, safe dialling) exists after ENG-12177 to ENG-12186, but there is no way for a rep to start or drive a session. Nothing is visible in the product.

### Solution

* A Call button at the top of saved contact views AND saved deal views.
* A session panel with: the current lead card, a queue preview with claim indicators ("being called by [rep]"), Pause, a manual Next Call button, a ring-time setting, a caller ID picker, and progress.
* Claim indicators come from polling `dialer.getActiveClaims` every 10 to 15 seconds. The 5 minute view sync can never power this. The server returns only claims on contacts visible in the caller's session and view scope, never all org claims.
* Manual Next Call works standalone: one click claims and dials the next lead through the ENG-12187 hooks. No automation is needed, which makes this ticket independently QA-able before the wrap-up ticket exists.
* Counts are shown as three separate numbers: source rows (rows in the view), unique dialable contacts (deduplicated people who have a phone number), and phoneless (rows with no callable number, surfaced, never silently dropped). Unique dialable contacts is the progress denominator.
* The panel shows a cursor-exhausted state: when the whole list has been loaded into the queue and worked, the rep sees a clear "queue complete" state. This is distinct from "all remaining leads are on calls with teammates, retry shortly", which shows a retry time instead.
* Session state lives in the URL (nuqs), so refresh and deep links restore the panel.
* PostHog activation tracking ships with this ticket, instrumented through the repo `instrument-activation-tracking` skill (never hand-written calls), at least `tool.opened`. Tracking only counts once the events are verified landing in PostHog.

**Technical notes**

* Launch surfaces: saved contact views and saved deal views (deal rows dial the resolved contact per ENG-12183's rule).
* Permission matrix: the button renders only with `FEATURES.POWER_DIALER` plus `voice.make_call`, and every procedure it calls rejects server-side without them, so hiding the UI is never the protection. Claim data is scoped server-side as above.

### Scope

* In: Call button on saved contact and deal views
* In: session panel (current lead, queue preview, claim indicators, Pause, manual Next Call, ring-time setting, caller ID picker, progress with the three count grains)
* In: cursor-exhausted state and leased-elsewhere retry state
* In: URL session state, refresh restore
* In: PostHog activation tracking, verified in PostHog
* Out of scope: wrap-up window and auto-advance (next ticket), Continue Calling chooser UI (next ticket, backend in ENG-12185), recovery and takeover screens (next ticket), voicemail drop (RCC 8)

### Acceptance criteria

 1. When a rep with the feature flag and calling permission opens a saved contact view or a saved deal view, a Call button is shown. Without the flag or permission, the button is absent AND direct calls to the procedures are rejected server-side.
 2. When the rep clicks Call, a session starts and the panel opens showing the current lead's name and number.
 3. When the panel shows progress, source rows, unique dialable contacts, and phoneless are displayed as separate numbers, and the progress denominator is unique dialable contacts.
 4. When another rep in the same shared view is on a lead, the queue shows "being called by [rep]" within 15 seconds.
 5. When the rep clicks Next Call, the next lead is claimed and dialled through the shared calling engine, with no auto-advance required. This works end to end before the wrap-up ticket ships.
 6. When every remaining lead is leased by teammates, the panel shows a retry message with a time, never a false "queue complete".
 7. When the whole list has been loaded and every item worked, the panel shows the complete (cursor-exhausted) state.
 8. When the rep changes ring time or caller ID, the next dials use the new values. Pause stops claiming.
 9. When the rep refreshes the page, the URL restores the session panel.
10. When the dialler is opened, a `tool.opened` event (at minimum) is sent via the repo instrumentation skill and is verified landing in PostHog before this ticket is called done.

### Design (Name 7)

* 27 · power dialer preflight — the launch modal: view name, in-scope / callable / excluded counts, skip reasons ("2 have no phone number, one is on the do-not-call list"), caller ID, queue order, **Start N calls**
* 28 · power dialer active — bottom bar — the session panel while dialling: bottom-docked, current lead + pipeline/stage, call controls, timer, End call

Launch entry point is the **Start Power Dialer** button in the list toolbar (visible in both frames). Full screen map on master ENG-12173.

relatedSnapshot.title: Make the power dialler the fastest way for our sales team to work their leads
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What we want

Make the power dialler the fastest way for setters, closers and confirmation reps to work their leads, so more new leads get called, more people show up and fewer inbound calls are missed. A rep presses Power dialler on any smart view and works the list on each person's own record, with a brief that answers why they're calling before the person picks up.

## Why

Since we moved our own sales team off Close, reps have used the power dialler once (one session, 28 Sep 2026). They make 9.5 calls a rep a day by clicking to call one lead at a time, against 43.9 on Close. All figures below are for our sales team's workspace, 13 Sep to 12 Oct 2026, from read-only production queries.

* **New leads go uncalled.** 4,534 of 7,520 new leads with a phone (60.3%) got no outbound call, and the ones called waited a median of 47.8 hours. Only 24 were called within 5 minutes.
* **Inbound callers are missed.** 185 of 242 inbound calls weren't answered.
* **Logging doesn't stick.** 3,206 of 3,371 auto-created call tasks are still open, and only 34 of 26,136 calls carry a deal.
* **Voicemail eats the day.** 54.3% of 2,111 calls since 18 Sep hit voicemail, and reps spent 13.2 hours listening to greetings.

This programme keeps the dialler we built and fixes what stops reps using it.

## How it should work

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Today
    A[Saved view] --> B[Session card on the list] --> C[Call] --> D[Rep opens the record to find context]
    E[Click-to-call] -. ignores the per-person hold .-> C
  end
  subgraph After
    F[Any smart view or calling list: Power dialler] --> G[Person's record: call bar, lead brief, outcomes]
    G --> H[Outcome books, re-queues or moves the deal] --> G
    I[Every call: power, click-to-call, inbound] --> J[(One hold per person and phone)]
  end
```

What changes for reps when everything here ships: a rep opens any smart view, or one of six ready-made calling lists (New leads, Due now, No-shows, Missed calls, Unconfirmed, Today's calls), and presses Power dialler. Each person opens on their own record with the call bar on top, a brief saying why now, what happened last, the money and what they said, and the outcomes on the right. Picking an outcome books, re-queues or moves the deal, then moves on after 1.5 s with Undo, never mid-note. New leads ring an available setter within minutes, unanswered inbound calls ring the rest of the team, and booked calls are confirmed by text before anyone calls.

Power sessions already hold each person for 3 minutes and show "Being called by" to other reps, with a team-wide 60-minute redial gap. The programme keeps that and extends it to every call.

Designs: James approved the kit designs on 15 Oct 2026. Clickable: Power dialler designs, private until James shares it. Each child carries its own screens; ENG-15220 has the session and the calling lists, and ENG-15465 has the lead brief.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Tickets grouped as parallel may start together when there's capacity, but they keep the priority order below. Waves show the earliest unlock, not a barrier: start a later ticket as soon as its own blockers are done. ENG-12188 and ENG-12468 sit under ENG-12173, and ENG-15236 is Aaron's; they're listed because this programme depends on them.

**Done:** ENG-15217, the next call waits for the rep, plus dialler tracking (shipped 14 Oct 2026), and ENG-12468, dial the number local time was worked out from.

### Wave 1: can start now

Parallel: ENG-15218, ENG-15236, ENG-15219 and ENG-12188.

1. ENG-15218: one caller per person on every call. In progress.
2. ENG-15236: every team People view can start the dialler. Unblocks ENG-15220.
3. ENG-15219: unanswered inbound calls ring the next free teammate.
4. ENG-12188: voicemail drop. No blocker in this programme.

### Wave 2: starts when ENG-15218 and ENG-15236 are done

5. ENG-15220: the session runs on each person's record, from any smart view, with the calling lists. Blocked by ENG-15218 and ENG-15236.

### Wave 3: starts when ENG-15220 is done

Parallel: ENG-15465, ENG-15221 and ENG-15222.

6. ENG-15465: the lead brief for each person. Blocked by ENG-15220.
7. ENG-15221: outcomes do the follow-up. Blocked by ENG-15220.
8. ENG-15222: attempt schedules and calling hours. Blocked by ENG-15220.

### Wave 4

Parallel: ENG-15224 and ENG-15223.

 9. ENG-15224: new leads called within minutes. Blocked by ENG-15220 and ENG-15222.
10. ENG-15223: confirmation by text first. Blocked by ENG-15220 and ENG-15221.

Cross-wave overlap: ENG-15219 may overlap ENG-15220, because inbound routing and the session don't share code paths.

## Decisions already made

* No separate Calling page. Sessions start from a smart view or an added calling list, and run on each person's record (James, 15 Oct 2026).
* Calling lists are normal views with rules that run on the server. Anyone can add one for themselves; admins can add one for the team.
* AI summaries for the lead brief are only regenerated when over 24 hours old or after new activity, and the cost is read after the first week.
* No parallel or predictive dialling. Our leads are fresh, and our research found the evidence favours one line per rep for warm leads.
* The session must work with answer detection on or off, and with each rep's Ring twice and automatic next call settings. ENG-15220 has the table.

## Not doing

* Local presence and number rotation. There's no independent evidence they raise pickups, so we'll revisit once tracking shows connect rate by number.
* Who works no-shows. Calling lists are added per team, so that's a floor decision, not a build.

## Open questions

* **Should** ENG-15235 **close once** ENG-15220 **ships?** Recommended: yes, because every call in a session shows the record. Aaron and James decide.

## Name 8 and rollback

Turning the dialler on for our sales team (the phone calling, power dialler and floor view flags) is a separate step after ENG-15218 and ENG-15236, with a named approver. Before ENG-15220 rolls out, the 22 callers with no team need a team, because calling lists are added per team. Each child ships off, or behind its own team setting, where it changes behaviour for reps.

## How we'll measure

Base: our sales team's workspace, read-only production replica, 13 Sep to 12 Oct 2026.

* Share of outbound calls placed from a session: 0% today (1 session). Target: over 50% within 14 days of ENG-15220 shipping. This is a business hypothesis; if it isn't reached, we interview reps before building more.
* Calls per active rep per day on our dialler: 9.5 today.
* New leads with a phone never called within 30 days: 60.3% today. Median hours to first call: 47.8 today.
* Inbound calls missed: 185 of 242 today.
* Calls tied to a deal: 34 of 26,136 today.

## Done when

- [ ] All nine children are done.
- [ ] A setter can press Power dialler on a team People view and be on a call within 2 clicks, on production.
- [ ] The measures above are read 14 days after ENG-15220 ships and posted on this ticket.

<details><summary>For whoever builds it</summary>

* Related programme: ENG-12173, the original dialler build, which delivered the session, queue and per-person hold this extends.
* Research behind this programme covered our call data, our dialler code at commits 076050116c and 28fcbd9b55, <domain>'s public app, Close's dialler docs and nine other diallers.
* Related: ENG-15235, ENG-15237, ENG-15159.

</details>

relatedSnapshot.title: Make dialling and calling work first time, every time
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What we want

Every outbound call, from the power dialler or by hand, rings the prospect on the first try, both people can hear each other, and a failure never leaves the rep stuck. When something does fail, we see it in minutes from our own data, not from a rep's message.

Reported by Name 9 in ENG-15734, and by Name 6, Name 10, Name 11 and Name 12 in #aqcuisity-migration and #app-acquisity-crm. Twelve read-only investigations on 20 Oct 2026 found the causes below. The evidence files sit in the CRM task folder `DIALLER-RELIABILITY-2026-10-20`.

## Why

Reps lose conversations and minutes every day, so fewer meetings get booked. 56 calling reports came in between 5 and 20 Oct (Slack, counted by the investigation, a floor). The balance check alone caused 24 refused calls on 19 Oct, about 8% of 301 calls that reached the answer step (Axiom, from ENG-15739). The same pattern already came back after three fixes (9, 9 and 16 Oct).

## How it should work

Three faults stack up. Only the AI Acquisition Sales Team uses funded calling (first admitted 5 Oct 2026), so it hit them first.

1. **The balance check is slow.** Each dial takes one shared workspace lock twice. Evening holds on 19 Oct had a median of 5 to 7.7 s and a p90 of 12 to 17 s, against 1.6 s that morning (Axiom).
2. **Late replies kill the call silently.** When our answer step replies after 14.9 s, Twilio ends the call: 18 of 18 such replies failed (Twilio records, 13 to 20 Oct). The rep hears nothing.
3. **Failures leave no trace.** Refused calls write no call row (63 in 7 days), and in the power dialler a refusal pauses the whole session as "paused by the user".

"Can't hear the prospect" has no proven cause yet. The leads are our ringtone stopping early and Safari speaker setup, and we have no audio data to settle it.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Rep clicks call] --> B[Token and balance check]
  B --> C[Twilio asks us how to route]
  C --> D[Answer step: balance check again]
  D --> E[Prospect rings]
  E --> F[Rep hears prospect]
  D -. refused .-> G[Session pauses, no record]
```

*Where the children change it: the answer webhook bound, the balance read made instant, parked holds cleared, the pause removed, telemetry added at every step, and the ringtone and audio path checked.*

When the whole programme ships: the balance check takes well under 100 ms, a refusal shows a clear Retry and keeps the session going, every attempt has a record with a reason, and a slow day raises an alert before a rep complains.

## Execution order

Updated 20 Oct 2026: consolidated from 9 children to 6 (ENG-15764, ENG-15769 and ENG-15770 folded into their siblings as duplicates), so fewer PRs, reviews and QA cycles.

**Shipped**

* ENG-15762: a refused call shows Retry and keeps the session going (PR Acquisity/Acquisity#7429).
* ENG-15768: the ringing tone plays until the prospect's audio starts (PR Acquisity/Acquisity#7430).
* ENG-15788: the dialler says why it is holding the next call (PR Acquisity/Acquisity#7437).

**In progress, ranked**

1. ENG-15763: the answer step always replies within 8 s (PR Acquisity/Acquisity#7435, waiting on review). Blocks ENG-15765's merge order only by shared files.
2. ENG-15765: the balance check becomes near-instant (query rewrite) and the parked holds are cleared. Rebases on ENG-15763.
3. ENG-15766: ring twice, closing the lead on session end, and a faster move to the next lead, in one PR extending Acquisity/Acquisity#7407.
4. ENG-15767: per-call summary, daily health check, outbound transcripts and the ring-timeout comparison. The per-call part builds on PR Acquisity/Acquisity#7385.

Safe together: ENG-15765, ENG-15766 and ENG-15767 touch different files (billing query, dialler wrap-up, telemetry and jobs). ENG-15765 rebases after ENG-15763 because both touch the answer route.

## Decisions already made

* James, 20 Oct 2026: make the balance check instant, with no lock and no loading state. Lean toward letting a call through when the check is slow.
* James, 20 Oct 2026: alerts only, no calling canary. Voice Insights goes on (James sets it up).
* James, 20 Oct 2026: full autonomy to build, QA and merge inside the standing merge rules, including UI changes, and to clear the parked holds after a dry run. The rep tickets and Slack feedback decide the UX.
* Owners: James and Ebubeker.

## Not doing

* A synthetic calling canary (James chose alerts only).
* Rebuilding the dialler UI. Anuj Bhatt's record-session and outcome PRs (Acquisity/Acquisity#7344 and Acquisity/Acquisity#7398) own that.

## Open questions

* Why database CPU rose from about 11% to 81 to 100% on 19 Oct beyond the two top queries. Recommended test: read the Axiom query-latency split by day after the Conversations fix ships. Decider: engineering.
* What breaks the audio on "can't hear" calls. Recommended test: Twilio Voice Insights for the 7 suspect calls from 19 Oct. Decider: James turns Voice Insights on.

## Done when

- [ ] Call-admission lock hold p90 is under 500 ms on a weekday evening, where it was 2.3 to 18.6 s on every weekday from 12 to 20 Oct (Axiom).
- [ ] No answer-step reply is above 10 s over 24 hours of real traffic, where 18 replies were at 14.9 s or more.
- [ ] Every refused call has a failed call row with a reason, where 63 in 7 days have none.
- [ ] The dialler health and session checks return clean for 3 days, where 14 sessions fail the session check today.
- [ ] Refused calls on the sales workspace stay under 1% of calls for 5 weekdays, where 19 Oct was about 8%. Read date to be set at release.

<details><summary>For whoever builds it</summary>

* The evidence: `findings/*.md` in the CRM task folder, plus `plan.md`.
* Related open work to coordinate with: ENG-15156 (PR Acquisity/Acquisity#7391, approved), ENG-15157 (PR Acquisity/Acquisity#7385, approved), ENG-15723 (PR Acquisity/Acquisity#7407), PRs Acquisity/Acquisity#7344 and Acquisity/Acquisity#7398.
* Axiom monitors named "Calling: ..." are created outside any PR.

</details>

relatedSnapshot.title: Log why each Power Dialer call is refused
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Why

17 of 33 refused Power Dialer calls between 13 and 19 Oct 2026 log only a bare `VoiceDialAuthorizationError` ("Power dial authorization failed" in Axiom), so we can't tell which check refuses them, and reps lose calls we can't explain or fix.

## What

* Every refusal in `authorizeAndBindPowerDial` and `authorizeOrdinaryBrowserDial` (`apps/web/lib/dialer/authorize-dial.ts`) carries a reason code, logged as the top-level `refusalReason` field: invalid_grant, from_mismatch, destination_mismatch, member_not_found, member_mismatch, voice_access_denied, session_missing, item_missing, session_member_mismatch, caller_id_not_owned, target_not_visible, caller_id_changed, browser_voice_unavailable, do_not_contact, funding_denied, contact_held, calling_policy, call_conflict (with `errorMessage`), invalid_signature, invalid_call_context, unexpected (with `errorName` and, for a TRPCError, `errorCode`).
* When the target is hidden, the log also says why (`targetVisibilityReason`, from `explainCurrentDialerTargetVisibility` in the new `target-visibility.ts`), whether the saved view's filters changed since the session last synced them (`filterSnapshotDrifted`, the same rule queue reconciliation uses before it rewrites the session snapshot), and whether the lead would still pass under the session's own filters (`visibleUnderSessionSnapshot`).
* The caller gets the same generic response as today.

## Lead hypothesis (medium-low confidence)

The visibility check rebuilds filters from the live saved view, not the session's snapshot (confirmed in code: `createDialerFilterSnapshot(view, …)` in `isCurrentDialerTargetVisible`). Name 6's shared view was edited 13 times on 19 Oct, so leads claimed under old filters may be refused. Relative-date filters such as lastTouchAt are the other suspect. The new fields separate the two. Changing the check to use the snapshot is a follow-up, because live re-reads may be how revoked access takes effect.

## Done when

* Unit tests assert each reason code through the logged fields, and a DB test proves drift and the session-snapshot recheck on a real edited view.
* After deploy, one day of Axiom has a non-null `refusalReason` on every "Power dial authorization failed" row, with a breakdown by reason, visibility reason and drift. An empty window is inconclusive.

relatedSnapshot.title: Tune power dialler ring time and the gap between calls

## What we want

Pick the power dialler ring timeout from data, and cut the wait between calls.

## Why

Delivers the speed part of ENG-15760. Power dialler no-answer was 30.7% against 11.5% for click-to-call (12 to 18 Oct, AI Acquisition Sales Team, prod query), with a 20 s or 32 s ring timeout. A 20 s timeout may cut calls off before anyone picks up, but that is a guess. Claiming the next lead to issuing its token takes a median 3.8 s (p90 8.1 s), and after an unanswered call the next call starts a median 22 s after the ring timeout with a 5 s auto-advance. Two steps in between run one after another and one is fetched twice.

## How it should work

Run 20 s against 32 s as a measured test on the sales workspace, then set the winner. Run the independent steps in parallel and fetch once.

## Not doing

* Refusal handling and the balance check.

## Done when

- [ ] A measured comparison of 20 s and 32 s ring timeouts (no-answer and answered-after-20 s counts) is attached.
- [ ] Claim-to-token median drops from 3.8 s and the gap after a no-answer drops from 22 s, each measured on a weekday.

relatedSnapshot.title: Power Dialler can ring a person twice before moving on
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A rep running the Power Dialler can turn on "Ring twice if no answer". When the first call to a person is not answered, the dialler calls them again straight away, once, before moving to the next person. Many people ignore the first call from an unknown number and pick up the second.

## Problem

Asked on the 30 Sep migration call by an SDR in AI Acquisition Sales Team: "Can you double dial with the Power Dialler? Ring up the person twice before moving on to the next lead." Today the Power Dialler calls each person once. To try again the rep has to stop, open the person and call by hand, which breaks the session.

## User experience

* In the Power Dialler session settings, next to ring timeout and auto-advance, there is a switch: **Ring twice if no answer**. It is off by default and remembered per rep.
* With it on, when a call ends without being answered the session card says "No answer. Calling again…" and the second call starts after a short pause, with a Skip button to move on instead.
* If the second call is not answered either, the session carries on as it does today: wrap-up, then the next person.
* If the first call is answered, goes to a voicemail the rep leaves a message on, or the rep ends it and picks an outcome, there is no second call.
* Both calls appear on the person's timeline as separate calls, and both count in the session summary as attempts. The person counts once.

## What's included

* The switch, the "calling again" state on the session card with Skip, and the second call.
* Not included: more than two attempts, a second attempt on a different number for the same person, and double dial for single calls made outside the Power Dialler.

## How it should work

* The second call goes through the same checks as any call: do not contact, opt-out, contact hours, phone funds and the rep's caller ID. If a check fails, the session moves on and says why.
* The person stays claimed by this rep between the two calls, so no other rep's session can pick them up in the gap.
* Pausing or ending the session during the gap cancels the second call.
* "Continue calling" still skips people attempted in the last hour, counting either attempt.

## Done when

- [ ] With the switch on, an unanswered first call is followed by one second call to the same person, and an unanswered second call moves on.
- [ ] An answered first call, or one the rep ends with an outcome, is not followed by a second call.
- [ ] Skip during the pause moves to the next person without calling again.
- [ ] With the switch off, the Power Dialler behaves exactly as today.
- [ ] A person marked do not contact between the two calls is not called again.
- [ ] Two reps running sessions on the same view never both call the person during the gap.
- [ ] Both calls show on the person's timeline, and the session summary counts two attempts and one person.
- [ ] Use of the switch is tracked through the repo's activation tracking skill, and the event is verified landing in PostHog.
- [ ] Live-call QA with a test number that does not answer, and one that answers on the second call.

## Open questions

* **What counts as "no answer".** Recommended default: the call ended without connecting (no answer, busy, or the ring timeout was reached). A carrier voicemail that picks up counts as answered, so it is not redialled, because the rep is already on the line with it.
* **Pause before the second call.** Recommended default: 3 seconds, not configurable.

## Implementation context

* Session settings today are auto-advance (on or off; 5, 10, 15 or 30 seconds) in `apps/web/lib/dialer/preferences.ts`, stored per rep per workspace in `dialer_user_preference`, and the ring timeout in `apps/web/lib/dialer/ring-timeout.ts`. The new switch belongs with them.
* The next person is claimed in `apps/web/lib/dialer/claim-next.ts` and an item is finished in `complete-item.ts`. The second attempt needs the item to stay claimed and not complete after the first unanswered call.
* Dial checks live in `authorize-dial.ts`, `dial-suppression.ts` and `do-not-contact-call.ts` and must run again for the second call.
* The session summary's no-answer counting is in `session-summary.ts`.
* A new column on `dialer_user_preference` is a small schema change.

relatedSnapshot.title: Keep the power dialler running when a call is refused, with a clear Retry
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What we want

When the phone balance check refuses or times out a call, the power dialler keeps the rep's session going and shows **Retry call** (and Skip), instead of pausing the whole session as "paused by the user".

## Why

Delivers the dialler part of ENG-15760. 33 calls were refused by our answer step between 13 and 19 Oct and left no record. 13 of them also paused the session, and the bar only offers Retry when a call never started (`controller-state.ts`, line 28). On 19 Oct Name 6 had 17 refusals in 3 hours across 7 sessions and made only 11 dialler calls (prod query, power-dialler investigation). Name 6 reported the same wait in ENG-15739: 1 to 2 minutes of dead time, and the only way out was Pause and skip the outcome.

## How it should work

A refused or busy call behaves like a call that never started: the lead stays with the rep, the bar says in plain words that the call did not connect and offers Retry call and Skip lead, and the session is not paused. The rep can dial the next lead within seconds. The exact wording and layout follow what reps said in the Slack reports and tickets.

## Not doing

* Fixing the cause of the refusals: ENG-15760 siblings own the balance check and answer step.
* Closing half-done leads when a session ends (its own sibling ticket).
* The record-session and outcome UI in Anuj's PRs Acquisity/Acquisity#7344 and Acquisity/Acquisity#7398.

## Done when

- [ ] A test fails today and passes after: a refused or busy outbound call leaves the session active and shows Retry call.
- [ ] The session invariant check shows 0 sessions paused by a refusal (13 in the 13 to 19 Oct data).
- [ ] The PR carries desktop and 375 px screenshots of the new bar state.

relatedSnapshot.title: Make the power dialler wait for the rep before calling the next person
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Part of ENG-15216. Reps have used the power dialler once since we moved off Close, so this makes a session safe to work in. The next call waits until the rep has finished, keys do the common actions, and the screen says why a session can't start. It also adds the dialler tracking every later child is measured with.

## Problem

* A 5-second auto-next countdown starts when the call ends. Typing a note, the text box and the Task or Book meeting dialogs don't pause it, so the next call starts mid-note.
* The Start button disappears without a reason when there's no saved view, a flag is off or a caller ID is missing.
* There are no keyboard shortcuts and no Skip button, and pausing comes in four different forms.
* With answer detection on, the dialler hangs up on voicemail and logs "Left voicemail" though nothing was left. The settings text says it "skips voicemail automatically".
* PostHog only records `tool.opened` and `enable_ring_twice` for the dialler.

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Today
    A[Call ends] --> B[Server saves result] --> C[5 s countdown] --> D[Next call, even mid-note]
  end
  subgraph After
    E[Call ends] --> F[Rep picks outcome] --> G{Typing or dialog open?}
    G -- no --> H[1.5 s with Undo] --> I[Next call]
    G -- yes --> F
  end
```

## What's included

* **Advance rule:** the queue moves only when the call has ended, an outcome and its required fields are saved, and no note, text box or dialog is open. Then 1.5 s with Undo; Undo can't run once the next dial starts. The 60 s server fallback for reps who walk away stays, but it pauses the session instead of dialling on.
* **Keys:** 1 to 9 for outcomes, S skip, N next, P pause, ? help. Keys are off while typing. One Pause control replaces the four.
* **Skip:** a Skip button wired to the existing skip action.
* **Honest voicemail copy:** the result reads "Voicemail, no message" when the dialler hung up, and the setting describes what it does.
* **Say why Start is missing:** every condition that hides Start shows a reason with a fix link instead.
* **Tracking:** PostHog events `dialler.session_started` (queue or view), `call.placed`, `call.connected`, `call.outcome` (with the outcome).

## Out of scope

* Lock override and idle-hold release tracking (`lock.override`): ENG-15218. It ships with the Call anyway and hold-release actions.
* New queues and the new call screen: ENG-15220.
* Voicemail drop: ENG-12188.

## Done when

* Typing a note or opening Book meeting during wrap-up never starts the next call. How to check: a unit test on the advance hold, and a browser check on a preview.
* Undo within 1.5 s keeps the rep on the same person, and no second call is placed.
* Every condition that blocks Start shows a reason instead of a missing button.
* The four PostHog events (`dialler.session_started`, `call.placed`, `call.connected`, `call.outcome`) land in PostHog from a preview session.

## Implementation context

Code at commit 076050116c: the countdown hold list is in `apps/web/components/crm/power-dialer/use-power-dialer-wrap-up-surface.ts` (around line 76), the countdown in `use-power-dialer-wrap-up.ts`, the server fallback in `apps/web/lib/dialer/call-status.ts`, and the voicemail setting copy in `apps/web/components/crm-v2/settings/phone-calling.tsx`.
